messages:
andrew: RFC follow-up for the disconnected-site packaging proposal — trying to capture the agent contract and delta/bundle format in one place. TL;DR: content-addressed chunk bundles + manifest v1 + agent-side two-phase apply + fallback to full blob. Looking for gaps and tradeoffs.

sara: +1 this aligns with the issues we've seen at a few customers with flaky WAN. Quick concern: how do we guarantee atomicity when a large model gets streamed in pieces?

jin: question: who is responsible for composing the delta bundles? server-side packager or an on-site build step? server-side means we can dedupe and compute chunk hashes once, but client becomes thin. client-side gives offline sites control but increases compute at the site.

maya: I sketched a manifest prototype that might help make the contract explicit. rough example:```
{
  "manifest_version": "v1",
  "bundle_id": "rb-2026-03-12-001",
  "created": "2026-03-12T18:22:00Z",
  "target_component": "inference-runtime",
  "policy": { "apply_mode": "two_phase", "max_retry": 3 },
  "chunks": [
    {"id":"sha256:aaa..","size":10485760,"compress":"zstd","type":"file-delta","offset":0},
    {"id":"sha256:bbb..","size":5242880,"compress":"zstd","type":"blob"}
  ],
  "signatures": [ {"alg":"ed25519","sig":"base64...","key_id":"infra-release"} ],
  "preflight": ["free_space>10%","k8s_ready","kvcache_healthy"]
}
```

maya: agent contract notes: 1) verify signatures before any write; 2) preflight checks pass or abort; 3) download chunks to staging path; 4) attempt apply to staging fs; 5) health-check rollback window; 6) commit swap.

andrew: exactly — want to make sure the swap/commit step is cheap (rename/flip symlink) so rollback is fast. For models we probably need an index that lets us fallback per-model: if chunk apply fails, fall back to previous stable model for that key instead of whole service restart.

luis: I can prototype the packager. plan: tar files, break into 4MB content-addressed chunks, zstd compress each, produce manifest. Server will keep chunk dedupe store and can serve via HTTP(s) + resume support. estimate ~2w.

kevin: security nit: we should standardize on signature envelope. COSE or RFC 7515? We need to support ed25519 (fast) and RSA-PSS (enterprise HSMs). Also include signer metadata + cert chain.

sara: operational tradeoff: pre-staging increases disk needs but makes apply predictable. for constrained appliances we should support streaming apply mode where chunks are applied as they arrive (with caveat of no atomic swap). That mode should be opt-in.

jin: interface boundary thought: split responsibilities: "packager" (server-side) exposes /manifest and /chunks endpoints; "agent" exposes a minimal management API: POST /bundles/apply {manifest_url, mode}. All orchestration (rollouts, canaries) stays in control plane. agent reports status back via heartbeat.

andrew: agreed. and add a small control surface for operator: `kubectl annotate node/edge-01 rbundle/apply=https://...` to trigger immediate apply for private installs. Example:```
kubectl annotate nodes edge-01 rbundle/apply="https://packages.redwood.local/rb-2026-03-12-001/manifest.json" --overwrite
```

ops-bot: automation: scheduled maintenance window set for 2026-03-20T02:00Z - will throttle chunk downloads during window. :gear:

kevin: telemetry: agent should emit metrics: bundle_fetch_seconds, chunk_download_errors_total, last_successful_apply_ts, last_failure_reason. Also log verification steps (signature_ok, preflight_ok).

luis: one other detail: allow a special chunk type "fast-path" which is a small metadata delta (e.g., config+tokenizer) so we can patch critical files without full model churn.

sara: rollback semantics we discussed: automatic rollback after N failed health checks (default N=3) within 10m. But operator can opt for manual rollback mode for sensitive sites.

jin: edge-case: intermittent connectivity — manifest should include an ordered list of chunk mirrors and optional resume token. Also include total_bundle_size so agent can decide pre-staging vs streaming.

andrew: final question for the thread: are we comfortable with the complexity of two apply modes (streaming vs pre-stage)? can we document clear operator guidance for when to pick each?

maya: I can put together a short decision table for the RFC appendix: when storage<20% => streaming, when latency sensitive => pre-stage, when regulatory immutable storage => pre-stage + signed immutability marker.

andrew: thanks — if no major objections I'll fold these decisions into the RFC patch and add a sample manifest schema + agent API. pls flag anything missing in the next 24h. :thumbsup:
